newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money recovers, other money rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money recovers, other money rates steady.

text.p: Dutch money rates were steady to a touch easier across the curve in lacklustre trade on Thursday, but overnight guilders climbed back to Tuesday's levels after Wednesday's fall.
Call money finished the day at 2.80 percent, after quoting at 2.68/81 bid-offer for most of the session, dealers said. On Wednesday call money fell to 2.62-68 percent bid-offer.
Dealers said there was no fundamental reason for the climb, just as there had been none for Wednesday's fall.
However, call money was considered relatively pricey compared to the current special advances rate of 2.50 percent.
Dealers said the day's activity had been concentrated at the short end of the money market curve.
One-month guilder deposits were down a single basis point at 2.70 percent bid, while three-month guilders eased fractionally to 2.74 percent bid.
The guilder was steady at 112.08 guilders per 100 marks.
